topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Combinations to Bases

sections.title: The Ingredients: Linear Combinations and Span
lecture_lines: Linear combinations scale and add vectors together.
Span is the total reachable territory.
Example: Two vectors cover the entire plane.
animations: Fade in text: 'Linear combination scales and adds vectors.'
Display two vectors v1, v2; show c1*v1 + c2*v2.
Animate scalar multiplication of vectors by c1, c2.
Show vector sum forming a parallelogram visually using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/parallelogram.svg].
Highlight the resulting spanned region in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Redundancy Test: Linear Dependence
lecture_lines: Linear dependence means redundant, wasteful vectors.
One vector can be formed by others.
Example: A third vector adds no reach.
animations: Fade in text: 'Linear dependence means redundant vectors.'
Show a vector v3 lying on the line of v1. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg]
Highlight relation v3 = c1*v1 with color #FF5555 using a drawing effect. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pencil.svg]
Display 'Redundant' label near the vector v3.
Fade out vector v3 to illustrate simplification.

sections.title: The Efficiency Expert: Bases
lecture_lines: Basis is the minimal set to span.
Basis is the most efficient instruction manual.
animations: Fade in text: 'A basis is a minimal spanning set.' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/manual.svg]
Show a set of linearly independent vectors.
Demonstrate that all vectors span the space.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
lecture_lines: Span is all you can reach.
Basis is the minimal toolset required.
These concepts define efficient vector spaces.
animations: Fade in text: 'Reviewing span, dependence, and basis concepts.'
